thread_title: People who started at 4lpa , and now earning more than 20 lpa , in less than 6 years , how did you all do it
comment:
I started with another 2 LPA in a service based company, in 2021. After two and half years (2023), I switched (with 4 LPA at that time) to a product company and got over 100% hike which amounted to about 10 LPA. 

While switching, I was mostly going through the system designing, code pattern and data structure concepts. It helped a lot. Don't forget to practice all this. 

After almost two and a half years again (2025), I switched (16 LPA at that time) to another product company (MNC) with around 32 LPA. I followed the same strategy and it worked.

The most important thing is to figure out what works the best for you and stick to it. Not limited to switching but while you're in the organization too! Find a niche, build a skill set in that niche and most importantly show your work!

thread_title: I'm so stupid, I think I ruined my career, pls tell options
comment:
Everyone else has covered the direct problem you have mentioned. I would like to mention an indirect one. 

This society has unfortunately drilled us since childhood that if we fail even once, our life is over. “Don’t play too much, you’ll fail in exams.” “Don’t roam around, if you don’t study, no one will like you.” “If you fail college, no one will give you a job.” etc. Everyone has gone through something like this in their childhood.

It’s like childhood is spent to tread a line of  life path where we never fail, otherwise the parents will be disappointed, the relatives will shame you, the teachers will see you as a ‘difficult kid’. This creates a fear of failure in our minds when we reach adulthood and then we never explore anything else other than that one path which is the safest. 

Life is meant for humans to make mistakes and learn from it and change our behaviour and be better. If we never failed, if we never changed anything in our lives, how would we know if we are better at something else. 

My story: I loved computer science in school, BTech in a different field, MTech in another totally unrelated field, changed my career path two times and now I am back to computer science. It’s like My 6-8 years of my studies and job were a waste. But I have learned so much, made many friends, met my now wife in that time, and so much more. It’s not failing, it’s life. 

Learn to understand this better, make mistakes, learn from it and move on. You’ll love it.

thread_title: Unpopular opinion: WITCH > FAANG when you factor in actually enjoying your life
comment:
Tools and technologies keep evolving, but core engineering principles stay the same.

Getting into FAANG-level companies is significantly more difficult than entering mass-hiring WITCH companies because the expectations around problem-solving, system design, and engineering depth are much higher.

One reason FAANG companies build many internal tools is to avoid relying heavily on third-party solutions for critical systems. At their scale, having in-house platforms gives them better control over reliability, customization, performance, and security.

The compensation levels also reflect these higher expectations and the scale of the engineering challenges involved.
